claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! You're welcome, I'm glad to help you with your Child Benefit query for Alex.

To continue assessing your eligibility, could you tell me: does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex lives with his mum rather than with you, I have a few more questions to understand your situation better.

Are you contributing towards the cost of looking after Alex, for example by paying maintenance or providing financial support for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - you know, helping with things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know you contribute financially towards Alex's care.

Could you tell me: is the amount you contribute at least the same as the current Child Benefit rate? (The current rate for an eldest or only child is £26.05 per week, or around £113 per month.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I pay £30 a week, so that's a bit more than that rate.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you, that's helpful to know you're contributing £30 per week.

One more important question: is Alex's mum (or anyone else who Alex lives with) already claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming Child Benefit for him. Nobody else is getting it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I have a couple more questions to complete my assessment.

Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not actually. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

Could you tell me a bit more about your situation abroad? Specifically:

1. Which country are you living in?
2. Are you working as a Crown servant (for example, working for the UK government abroad, such as in the armed forces or diplomatic service)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living in Spain at the moment. And no, I'm not a Crown servant - I'm not working for the UK government or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you're living abroad in Spain and not working as a Crown servant, I have one more question:

Do you have either settled status or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme? Or are you perhaps still registered or have ties to the UK in another way (for example, are you still paying UK National Insurance contributions or do you have a UK employer)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme. I'm just living in Spain now - I'm not paying UK National Insurance or working for a UK employer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:
- Alex is 9 years old and lives with his mum in the UK
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit rate)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You are living in Spain, not as a Crown servant
- You don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You're not paying UK National Insurance or working for a UK employer

Unfortunately, one of the core eligibility requirements for Child Benefit is that **you must live in the UK**. While there are some exceptions (such as being a Crown servant or living in certain countries with specific qualifying circumstances), based on what you've described, these exceptions don't appear to apply to your situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Reason:**
While you meet several of the criteria – Alex is under 16, you contribute more than the Child Benefit rate towards his upkeep (£30 per week), and no one else is claiming for him – there is a fundamental requirement that **you must live in the UK** to qualify for Child Benefit.

Since you're living in Spain and don't fall into any of the exceptions (such as being a Crown servant or having EU settled/pre-settled status with qualifying circumstances), you unfortunately cannot claim Child Benefit.

**However**, it may be worth noting that Alex's mum, who Alex lives with in the UK, may be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him instead. If she's a UK resident and responsible for Alex, she could potentially make a claim.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?
